fieldMarks: Small tree squirrel, 11-13 in including tail; far smaller than a gray squirrel.
Rusty-olive to reddish upperparts and a white or cream belly, separated in summer by a dark side stripe.
White eye ring year-round; ear tufts in winter.
Tail smaller and flatter than other tree squirrels', orange-red to yellowish-gray, often with a black band.
behavior: Active by day and noisy: rattles, screeches, growls, buzzes and chirps used to defend territories year-round.
Harvests conifer cones in late summer and autumn and stores them in central middens; cone cuttings on stumps and rocks are common sign.
Eats mainly conifer seeds plus many mushrooms, buds, fruit, sap, insects and occasionally bird eggs or young snowshoe hares.
habitat: Boreal coniferous forest with abundant seeds and interlocking canopy, also hardwood and mixed forests in the east; can live in suburbs and towns where suitable conifers remain.
range: Wide North American range: spruce forest over most of Alaska, the boreal and western coniferous forests, and eastern hardwood forests, extending south along mountain ranges at the southern and eastern edges of its range.

lookalikes.name: Douglas squirrel
lookalikes.howToTell: Where ranges meet, the red squirrel's underside is white or cream, while the Douglas squirrel's is rust-coloured.
